entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kātyāyana or Mahākātyāyana was a disciple of Gautama Buddha, one of the ten principal disciples, and foremost in expanding on and explaining brief statements of the Buddha.

He was born in the 5th century BCE in present-day India and died in the 4th century BCE.

Kātyāyana is listed in the Pali Canon as one of the principal disciples who received the Dhamma from the Buddha himself, and was known for his exceptional memory and ability to recall the Buddha's teachings.

Kātyāyana was also a key figure in the development of the Mahayana tradition, which emphasized the ideal of the Bodhisattva and the attainment of enlightenment for the benefit of all sentient beings.
